notes:
The manuscript pagination is 102, in pale writing at the lower-left edge; the scan is 103. There is no visible date or title on this leaf. A short horizontal separator is at the top centre.

The opening space is X_C(C), with an inserted X=. This is a visual decision from the subscript, not a normalization to an expected analytic-space notation.

The interlinear morphism stroke is literally a dash without a discernible arrowhead. The fact that the following phrase calls it a K-morphisme suggests an intended arrow, but the transcription preserves the observed dash.

At the first raised T adjacents, both witness hyphens were removed because the round mark before djacents is the initial a, not a dash. The later main-line T adjacents also lacks a hyphen. The genuine hyphen in T-adjacence and the quoted T-horizontal remain.

The left-margin wording is not securely expanded: the image shows en supp... and a compressed ending. The proposed abbreviated first reading is explicitly doubtful, with C's full en supposant as alternative. The formula x',y'∈X'_barK is readable.

The short cancellation before Π₁ might conceal ∈, or it may be a cancellation flourish. It is retained as a doubtful deleted sign, and requires the main reader's decision. No mathematical argument is used to force it.

The cancelled right-side block contains a first line before T which neither witness adequately records. The possible le and de are kept doubtful; the intervening crossed word is physically obscured at the enlarged view. T qui passe par x',y' is substantially more legible. The whole block is treated as cancelled, including the lower x',y', rather than a live added qualification.

The source has a colon after comparer and the cancelled formula. The source wording is preserved even though ordinary French might call for à.

Pi notation is context-sensitive on this leaf: Π in Hom denotes the groupoid, while π in the membership displays denotes a fundamental group. The handwritten shapes in both uses are roof-and-two-leg forms, so the upper/lower-case allocation uses the local mathematical role together with the witnesses, not an asserted visual distinction of letter size alone.

Both (53) and the membership line visibly use g with x,y, without prime strokes. In (54), the left g instead has y',x' and the right g has y,x. These source indices are preserved. I have not harmonized them to a single convention.

The T arguments in the membership display are written ux',uy', without separate inner parentheses. In the explanatory text below, u(x'),u(y') has parentheses. This local difference is preserved.

The first annotation word is read strate, not H's structure. Its middle a is very compressed and dot-like; the full-reading confidence is medium. A possible abbreviated str.te cannot be excluded solely from this leaf, but no additional expansion has been introduced in the proposed text.

The author's conditional/doubt wording includes « on ne peut affirmer que ... soient encore T adjacents », « Mais s'ils le sont », and « qui est défini par hyp. d'horizontalité ». These are transcribed source qualifications, not reports of a proof check by this reader.

H's supplied expansions and editorial relecture/note comments are not copied as source text. In particular loc\supplied{alemen}t is treated as editorial representation of the visible abbreviation, not an independent source-reading discrepancy. H's ens\supplied{emble} differs substantively because the source letters are nb.

A formal naturality/cancellation check was actually performed, as recorded below. It verifies a refined conditional statement and does not prove all the geometric hypotheses used on the manuscript page or resolve the source's index conventions.

Original image viewed once; each supplied half viewed once. Each of ten newly created tight crops was viewed once. Crops use original pixel boxes, LANCZOS enlargement to 3000-pixel width, autocontrast, and mild unsharp masking; the margin crop alone was rotated clockwise 26 degrees. No OCR, external research, other-page reading, or LaTeX compilation was used.

check_events.statement: For a functor F of groupoids commuting with u, assume F sends both chosen horizontal paths l_{b,a} and l_{ub,ua} to the corresponding chosen paths. If the comparison factor is defined by {}^u l_{b,a}=g_{b,a}(u)l_{ub,ua}, then F(g_{b,a}(u))=g_{Fb,Fa}(u).
check_events.outcome: Verified by applying F to the defining equality, replacing the images of the two chosen paths using the stated assumptions, and right-cancelling the invertible horizontal path. The compatibility assumptions were explicit hypotheses of this check; their geometric realization and the precise indexing convention in (53) were not independently established.
